author: translator-agent
title: TranslatorService and LanguagesUtil split out of SymbolicLM
body:
Owner decisions of 2026-09-29 (relayed by the orchestrator): translation moves out of SymbolicLM into a dedicated TranslatorService (lib/translator-service/) with pluggable backends; language identification and spelling also move out into a dedicated LanguagesUtil (lib/languages-util/). Final separation: LanguagesUtil = language id (token/message, plus matrix-language/frame detection for mixed rows) + spelling; TranslatorService = translation backends (may call LanguagesUtil to decide what to translate); SymbolicLM = UD parsing + SOP generation + uncertainty + routing that calls the other two.

Done: lib/symbolic-lm/translate.mjs + english.mjs moved unchanged to lib/translator-service/backends/symbolic.mjs + english.mjs, exposed through a loadBackend(name) registry in lib/translator-service/index.mjs (symbolic wired in; opus-mt and apertium registered as research backends, not yet implemented). lib/symbolic-lm/langid.mjs and lib/spellfix.mjs (+lib/spellfix/) moved unchanged to lib/languages-util/langid.mjs and spellfix.mjs; added lib/languages-util/frame.mjs (detectFrame, Myers-Scotton matrix-language-frame heuristic over functionLanguage() token classification) for the mixed-message matrix route of the upcoming comparison. SymbolicLM's own index.mjs now only imports these two components and no longer contains translation or language-id code.

Behaviour preservation, both moves: ran node tools/symbolic-lm.mjs english --in <50 fresh formalizer-v1 dev rows> --out ..., with and without --spell, through the current (moved) code, then temporarily restored the pre-move file layout (old import paths, old ROOT calculation in spellfix.mjs) and re-ran the identical command; diffed the two outputs each time and got byte-identical results in all cases (translate-only move: 50/50 identical; langid+spellfix move: 50/50 identical with and without --spell). tests/symbolic-lm.test.mjs's recorded-Stanza-parse replay test (no live Python needed) and the moved-out tests/translator-service.test.mjs (English morphology, never-guesses-an-unknown-word) pass unchanged. tests/model-input-boundary.test.mjs, tests/no-context-lint.test.mjs, tests/wire-help.test.mjs and node tools/check-spec-refs.mjs all pass after the move.

Docs: DS021 gained a LanguagesUtil section and a rewritten TranslatorService section (SymbolicLM's own section trimmed to UD parsing/SOP generation/uncertainty/routing only); docs/runtime.html and docs/wiki.html got matching sections/terms; dependencies.md got a LanguagesUtil section (moved from the old 'Spelling-correction resources' section) and an updated TranslatorService section.

author: translator-agent
title: eval-translator-compare-v1 results and Q-PIPE-1 decision
body:
Apertium dropped before running: no Romanian-English pair exists, packaged (apt) or in the apertium GitHub organization's 655 repositories (checked 2026-09-29; apertium-ron is a monolingual analyzer only).

Romanian (150 fresh formalizer-v1 train.jsonl rows, dev fully consumed by eval-symbolic-lm-v1): direct 26.0/27.3% (strict/tolerant); symbolic 23.3/29.3%; symbolic-hybrid 26.0/32.0%; opus-mt 8.0/12.0%. Paired vs direct (tolerant): symbolic +2.0 [-4.7,+8.7]; symbolic-hybrid +4.7 [-1.3,+10.7]; opus-mt -15.3 [-22.7,-8.0] (decisive against). No arm's lower 95% CI bound over direct is above 0; opus-mt about 6x slower than direct and slower than the symbolic backend too. This is the second independent experiment (after eval-symbolic-lm-v1) to find the same thing.

Mixed (100 rows): direct 37.0/37.0%; symbolic and symbolic-hybrid both 43.0/44.0%; opus-mt 28.0/30.0%; matrix (new frame-language route) 34.0/34.0%. Paired vs direct (tolerant): symbolic/symbolic-hybrid +7.0 [0.0004, +14.0] (unrounded lower bound essentially exactly zero -- the closest possible miss of the decisive threshold); opus-mt -7.0 [-17.0,+2.0]; matrix -3.0 [-8.0,+1.0].

Owner question 1 (can Opus-MT clean romgleza into fluent English?): manual reading of all 50 opus-mt outputs of the mixed stage-50 sample: 21/50 (42%, Wilson 95% CI [29%,56%]) fully fluent, no residual untranslated Romanian. The rest keep a short Romanian function word/discourse marker/verb (Vreau, Poti, Cine, Deci, Adica, Colegul, Scriu, Pregatesc) or a whole subordinate clause untranslated when English dominates the sentence -- the model was not trained on code-switched input. An automatic langid-residual proxy overcounts fluency (38/50) because its neighbor-smoothing was built for original mixed text, not post-MT leftovers; the manual number is the one that answers the question. Answer: no, not reliably.

Owner question 2 (unknown/niche words, 40-message hand-written probe, 57 judged word instances/backend): symbolic 40 correct/12 copied/2 hallucinated/2 dropped/1 transliterated (70/21/4/4/2%); opus-mt 18 correct/21 copied/12 hallucinated/6 dropped/0 transliterated (32/37/21/11/0%). The symbolic backend's 'never guess' design shows: unknown words are copied and reported untranslated, known niche/technical terms (bormasina->drill, uzucapiune->usucapion, cadastru->cadastre, grefier->registrar) are usually correct. Its two hallucinations are real dictionary-entry bugs (girant->manager instead of guarantor; user->royal curt usher instead of user), not guessing -- flagged as a follow-up, not fixed here. Opus-mt hallucinates about 5x as often (scadenta->'invoice number... number one', sifonul->'the whistle', catun->'the pail', polizorul->'the angler', tabloul(panel)->'the electric painting'). Pipeline-level finding (not a translator behaviour): protect.mjs's name-masking checks a sentence-initial capitalized word only against an English common-word list, so it mismasks an ordinary Romanian common noun at a Romanian sentence's start (Clanta->Ent1); a follow-up, not fixed here.

Decision (Q-PIPE-1, preregistered rule): Romanian's default route changes from translate to direct (lib/symbolic-lm/index.mjs DEFAULT_ROUTES; the rule's explicit Romanian fallback applies since nothing beat direct decisively). Mixed messages keep their current default (translate, symbolic backend): the evidence for switching is not decisive (CI lower bound essentially exactly 0), which is the rule working as designed, not a null result being ignored. Opus-MT and Apertium are not adopted anywhere; the new matrix route is not adopted (kept as a research backend). Both Q-SLM-1 and Q-PIPE-1 (the same underlying open question) removed from questions.md; recorded in DS021, CHANGES.md, PAS_TASK.md.

author: clean-english-ui-agent
title: textToCleanEnglish stage-1 survey: symbolic backend has best meaning preservation, LLMs more fluent but hallucinate more
body: Small (n=40/bucket), heuristic-only cross-check of 4 backends for the owner's proofread+translate+simplify UI step (status/preregistrations/text-to-clean-english-v1.json, status/experiments.json text-to-clean-english-v1): the already-shipped symbolic backend (LanguagesUtil spellfix + TranslatorService dictionary translation, no LLM) has the best or tied-best meaning-preservation rate on every bucket (noisy_en 100%, mixed 82.5%, ro 72.5%) and stays well inside a 2s UI budget (57-509ms), at the cost of a lower fully-English rate on Romanian (65%, visible untranslated words). Gemma-3-1b-it and Qwen3-1.7B (zero-shot, one combined 'clean' prompt) reach higher English fluency (87.5-100%) but measurably worse meaning preservation, worst for gemma3-1b on mixed text (55%). Opus-MT (translation only) underperforms symbolic on meaning preservation on both ro and mixed, consistent with the owner's prior note that it hallucinates. Recommendation direction: symbolic first for noisy English and probably ro/mixed too, LLM only as an escalation for rows the symbolic path leaves with untranslated words or unparsed spans; the owner's mandatory accept/edit/reject step is well justified since even the best backend here changes meaning on a nontrivial minority of ro/mixed rows. Stopped at stage 1 (not extended to 100/bucket, LanguageTool/Gemma-3-4B/Claude Haiku not run) because a concurrent duplicate agent instance was found already running a larger, more thorough version of this same survey; see the process journal entry and topic note server-and-ui for the duplicate-agent situation.

author: clean-english-ui-agent
title: LanguageTool 5.9 runs on the host Java 8; corrupts unmasked proper names
body: For text-to-clean-english-v1: LanguageTool 6.x needs Java 17 (confirmed separately), but the older LanguageTool 5.9 (from https://languagetool.org/download/archive/LanguageTool-5.9.zip, the only remaining source for pre-6.0 releases) runs fine under the hosts existing OpenJDK 8, as long as it is started via its plain org.languagetool.server.HTTPServer class rather than the jars default HTTPSServer main class (which demands a --config/TLS setup and exits under any Java version). Verified with a real /v2/check request. Latency ~50-110ms/request, well inside the ~2s UI budget. However, run unmasked (no protect.mjs) against the surveys 20-row already-clean control set, its top-suggestion auto-apply corrupts unrecognized proper names: Emeka to EMEA, Alba Iulia to Alba Julia, Otieno to Orient, Turcanu to Tuscany. This matches lib/text-to-clean-english/backends/languagetool.mjs doc comments stated rationale for masking names/numbers before calling it, now with a concrete measurement from an independent run.

author: clean-english-ui-agent
title: Independent backend survey for textToCleanEnglish (130 rows, GPU+CPU, real execution)
body: Sample: 40 Romanian + 40 mixed + 50 noisy-English rows (incl. 10 from datasets_sources/new_cases/raw, typos/casual_register categories), seeded draw from datasets/formalizer-v1 dev (no eval/suites row used). Backends run with real inference (not simulated): EuroLLM-1.7B-Instruct, Qwen3-1.7B, Gemma-3-1b-it via training/python/proofread_llm.py in ~/nlp-venv (GPU, greedy, batch 16, one combined proofread+translate+simplify prompt); Opus-MT (Helsinki-NLP/opus-mt-ROMANCE-en) via lib/translator-service/backends/opus-mt.mjs translateBatch (CPU, ~mt-venv); LanguageTool 6.6 via a freshly downloaded portable Temurin 17 JRE (system Java is only 8) on ro/mixed/noisy_en with automatic top-suggestion correction. Automated proxy metrics (not the full SymbolicLM/gold-SOP oracle the task asked for -- time-boxed): numbers preserved, question-mark preserved, proper-noun-token overlap (diacritics-folded), LanguagesUtil identify() English purity, length ratio, unchanged rate. Results (aggregate n=130 for the 3 LLMs, n=79 for opus-mt ro+mixed, n=50 for LanguageTool noisy_en): EuroLLM numbers 100%/question 96%/nouns 73%/purity 98%, best overall balance but showed a real instruction-echo hallucination failure mode on gibberish/very-short degenerate input (echoes its own system prompt back) and length blew up 2-4x on a few long multi-fact rows. Qwen3-1.7B numbers 99%/question 95%/nouns 82%/purity 93%, but left 3-8% of ro/mixed rows completely untranslated (unchanged output) -- least reliable translator of the three. Gemma-3-1b-it numbers 99%/question 96%/nouns 65%/purity 98%, fastest (0.25s/row GPU), but on one long multi-sentence Romanian row it silently truncated to only the LAST part of the message, dropping earlier stated facts -- a real meaning-loss failure mode, not just a fluency one. Opus-MT: nouns 92% (best, from protect.mjs-style masking upstream), purity 98%, but slow on CPU (~2s/message, at the UI's 2s budget) and translation-only (no grammar/simplification). LanguageTool: fast (mean 80ms, p95 191ms), zero-hallucination on genuine English, but corrupts foreign-language tokens if applied unmasked to mixed text (measured: 'aplicația de rezervări' -> 'application de reservoir') -- confirms it must only ever see text the gate has classified purely English, which is exactly how lib/text-to-clean-english/backends/languagetool.mjs is built (masks names/numbers/quotes with protect.mjs regardless, and DS012/dependencies.md already document the unmasked-corruption finding independently). Claude Haiku: could not run -- an OpenRouter API call (using the pre-set OPENROUTING_API_KEY env var) was blocked by the sandbox's own auto-mode exfiltration-scouting classifier; not retried through another channel per its instructions. Gemma-3-4B-it: not downloaded (time budget). This cross-checks and is broadly consistent with the other concurrent instance's own smaller stage-1 finding (status/experiments.json text-to-clean-english-v1) that the shipped symbolic backend has the best meaning preservation of the low-cost options, and adds a documented, reproducible hallucination-failure-mode catalogue (echo, truncation, silent no-op) for the three LLM candidates that any future 'llm' backend default (questions.md Q-CLEAN-1) should guard against with a sanity check, not just trust.

author: clean-english-ui-agent
title: textToCleanEnglish survey scored: gate, LanguageTool (masked) for English, Qwen3-1.7B GGUF (masked) for Romanian and mixed
body: Scored survey text-to-clean-english-v1 (inference only, small samples, 10 to 44 rows per cell; intervals in summary.md). Recommended default: gate, then LanguageTool 5.9 masked for English, then Qwen3-1.7B Q8_0 masked for Romanian and mixed (config/text-to-clean-english.json, llm.model qwen3-1.7b-base). Evidence: on the owner's independent noisy-English drafts (170 rows with reference rewrites) exact match is 1% untouched, 12% symbolic spelling, 24% LanguageTool masked, 31% Qwen3 masked; on generator noise the three cleaners raise SymbolicLM = gold by 17 to 23 points over the original and are not separable. Unmasked LanguageTool keeps names in only 43% of noisy rows (masked 97%). Romanian and mixed: clean parse and English 70% and 64% with the masked LLM against 3% and 14% untouched, but SymbolicLM = gold on Romanian falls from 48% to 28% because the gold keeps Romanian words, so the automatic score cannot judge that path; its value is the user's review. The gate sends 0 of 300 clean dev rows and 9 of 400 independent clean drafts to a backend. Median CPU latency 59 ms (LanguageTool), 561 to 638 ms (LLM). Caveats: the shipped prompt and Romanian-aware masking were iterated on the evaluation rows (optimistic), GPU batch-1 latency and Gemma 3 4B were not run, Haiku is n=10 per bucket.

author: clean-english-ui-agent
title: textToCleanEnglish: three defects found while scoring the production path
body: 1) A backend that answered with no text (gemma-3-270m-base, the translate default, on Romanian) was shown to the user as an empty proposal that deleted the whole message; now a failed backend, degraded to no change. 2) protect() masked sentence-opening Romanian words (Verifica, Spune-mi, Inseamna) as names, so the model never saw them and they stayed untranslated; protect() now takes an isCommon hook and the llm backend passes the Romanian lexicon for non-English text. 3) Qwen3 prefixed its answer with an empty think block; the backend strips it and asks llama-server for enable_thinking false. Also: LanguageTool masked/unmasked behaviour reproduced (unmasked corrupts names).
